newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt says by-election win unlikely.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt says by-election win unlikely.

text.p: The Liberal Party, part of the Australian coalition government, said it was unlikely to retain the federal seat of Lindsay in the by-election on October 19.

Federal director Andrew Robb said the opposition Labor Party's deal to swap preference votes with the anti-immigration party, Australians Against Further Immigration, boosted its chances of success in the by-election.
"This sleazy preference deal will mean that it's almost near impossible for us to hold this seat," Robb told reporters.
He said the anti-immigration party's preferences were likely to translate into about 6,000 votes for Labor.

"We need 1,000 votes to switch back to Labor and under this preference deal, there's every prospect that ... unwittingly people voting for the Australians Against Further Immigration will be voting for the Labor Party in the Lindsay by-election," Robb said.
Former minister Ross Free, who lost the western Sydney seat in the March 2 election to the governing Liberal-National coalition, remains Labor's candidate.
The High Court of Australia ordered the by-election in September after Liberal candidate Jackie Kelly was found ineligible under the constitution.
Kelly was a government employee and held dual Australian-New Zealand nationality when she stood for a seat in parliament's lower house, the House of Representatives.
She is again standing as the Liberal candidate in the by-election after meeting constitutional requirements.
Opposition leader Kim Beazley said in September the Labor Party would find it difficult to win back the seat.
